rule: Never use string formatting to build SQL queries
Use bcrypt or argon2 for password hashing
Never use pickle.load on untrusted data
Always use os.path.realpath and validate against allowed base dir
Load secrets from environment variables
Never use eval() or Function() with user input
good_example: Use JSON.parse() for data; never execute user strings

rule: Never set innerHTML with untrusted data
Never use jwt 'none' algorithm; always verify signature
Never hardcode secrets in client-side JS
good_example: Use process.env.API_KEY and never expose in frontend bundle

rule: Reject dangerous keys before merging untrusted objects
good_example: Validate against a strict schema and reject __proto__, prototype, and constructor keys

rule: Always type request user and validate ownership
good_example: router.get('/item/:id', auth, (req: AuthRequest, res) => { Item.findById(req.params.id, {owner: req.user.id}) })

rule: Never use $_GET/$_POST directly in queries
Validate file type by MIME + extension
good_example: $finfo = new finfo(FILEINFO_MIME_TYPE); validate mime; use uniqid() name; store outside webroot

rule: Use PreparedStatement not Statement
bad_example: stmt.execute('SELECT * FROM u WHERE id=' + id)
good_example: PreparedStatement ps = conn.prepareStatement('SELECT * FROM u WHERE id=?'); ps.setInt(1, id)

rule: Never deserialize untrusted data with ObjectInputStream
good_example: Use JSON (Jackson) with strict type handling; implement look-ahead deserialization filter

rule: Use parameterized queries with database/sql
bad_example: db.Query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id=' + id)
good_example: db.Query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id=?', id)

rule: Use crypto/rand not math/rand for security-sensitive values
Use strong parameters / permit whitelist
Use parameterized queries with SqlCommand
bad_example: new SqlCommand('SELECT * FROM u WHERE id=' + id, conn)

rule: Never log sensitive fields
good_example: logger.info(f'Login attempt: user={username}')  # never log password

rule: Treat LLM output as untrusted before using downstream
good_example: # Parse + validate structured output; never exec/eval LLM text

rule: Never interpolate untrusted content directly into prompts as instructions
good_example: Use clear delimiters + system/user role separation; treat retrieved docs as data not instructions

rule: Django - keep DEBUG=False and never expose SECRET_KEY in prod
Django - use ORM not raw() to avoid SQL injection
good_example: User.objects.filter(id=id)  # or raw with params list

rule: Flask - set SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY and SECURE
Express - use helmet for security headers
good_example: app.use(helmet()); // sets CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options etc.

rule: Express - validate input with zod/joi; never trust req.body
Never render LLM output as HTML without sanitization
Pin dependencies and commit lockfile
Rails - use strong params and avoid html_safe on user input
Laravel - use Eloquent/query builder not DB::raw with input
Spring - enable CSRF protection and method-level @PreAuthorize
Use html/template not text/template for web output
Fail closed - deny by default on errors not allow
Never expose stack traces or internal errors to users
Use atomic DB operations for balance/inventory updates
good_example: UPDATE accounts SET bal=bal-? WHERE id=? AND bal>=?  // atomic

rule: Verify object ownership on every API request (prevent BOLA)
Always validate OAuth state and use exact redirect_uri
good_example: Whitelist exact redirect_uri; validate state param matches

rule: Use bounds-checked APIs and validate lengths before every memory operation
good_example: Validate input length and use a bounded operation sized to dst

rule: Prefer RAII containers and smart pointers over raw ownership
bad_example: char* p = new char[n]; delete[] p;

rule: Minimize unsafe blocks and document invariants at each unsafe boundary
good_example: Use safe APIs; isolate unavoidable unsafe code and test its invariants

rule: Threat-model high-risk workflows before implementation
bad_example: Build payment flow without abuse cases or trust boundaries
good_example: Document assets, trust boundaries, abuse cases, controls, and negative tests

rule: Generate an SBOM and verify release provenance
bad_example: Deploy artifact with unknown transitive dependencies
good_example: Generate SBOM; sign artifact; verify provenance before deploy

rule: Run secret scanning and revoke exposed credentials
bad_example: Remove leaked key from latest commit only
good_example: Revoke key immediately; scan history; remediate exposure; prevent recurrence

rule: Prevent public and wildcard cloud permissions by policy
good_example: Use least-privilege actions and resources; enforce policy-as-code checks

rule: Define and test retention and deletion for sensitive data
bad_example: Keep all user data and backups indefinitely
good_example: Set approved retention; test deletion across primary data, caches, and backups

rule: Add negative authorization tests for every protected resource
bad_example: Test only that the owner can access the object
good_example: Test unauthenticated, wrong-user, wrong-role, and cross-tenant access

rule: Design credentials and sessions for rapid revocation
bad_example: Long-lived credentials cannot be centrally revoked
good_example: Use short-lived credentials and tested centralized revocation procedures

rule: Never pass user-controlled input as a Jinja2/Mako template string
Never use template literals or eval to render user input as server-side template logic
good_example: Use a sandboxed expression evaluator; never eval user strings

rule: Type-check MongoDB query fields to prevent operator injection
